name: Hiri Current
scope: Broad Hiri naming convention: northward Australian boundary branch from an OSW 15 S bifurcation approach, clockwise around the Gulf of Papua entrance, to an OSW eastern Louisiade approach. Excludes closed gyre return circuits, direct mid-basin Solomon inflow, EAC, downstream New Guinea currents and eddy excursions. Narrower literature uses Hiri only south of PNG and proposes Gulf of Papua Current for the connected boundary system; no alias merge or complete system extent admitted.
layer: Upper-ocean regional geography; no fixed-depth current core or vertically integrated streamline reconstructed. Source northern bifurcation descriptions have different depth support.
time_convention: Regional naming convention drawing on 2018 modeled context and 1993 circulation descriptions; not one simultaneous dated field, an annual mean route or seasonal length measurement.
source_locator: Section 1 and section 3.1.5: northward branch initiated near 15 S, clockwise Gulf of Papua circulation and depth dependence. Figure 1 separates upper 0-300 m and deeper modeled flows.
source_citation: Wijeratne et al. (2018), Estimates of Surface and Subsurface Boundary Current Transport Around Australia, Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans 123, 3444-3466, doi:10.1029/2017JC013221.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects all offshore vertices and the eastern Louisiade gate. Nominal start near 15 S follows Wijeratne; alternative 18 S start follows the broader Oliver and Holbrook regional description. These are source-specific geographic conventions, not equivalent-depth observations or statistical endpoints. The route does not trace a source gyre or transit track.
scenario_rule: Two source-specific origin conventions crossed with longitude and independent endpoint latitude offsets: 54 editorial scenarios, not statistical uncertainty.

alternative_routes.interpretation: Broader 18 S regional origin convention; no inference of one fixed layer or seasonal transition.
